title: Robust quant calibration feedback loop for per-block scale stabilization (Llama/Mistral/Qwen)
creator: Ling Zhang
description: Introduce a model-specific calibration and validation pipeline that reduces accuracy regressions caused by activation outliers and unstable layer scales when converting to FP8/INT8. Focus is on per-block (transformer block / attention block) attenuation maps, attention-head clipping heuristics, and an automated feedback loop that updates scale maps based on periodic validation runs for Llama, Mistral, and Qwen families. Goal: preserve generation quality within a small delta while achieving INT8/FP8 cost targets.
acceptance_criteria: Calibration pipeline produces stable per-block scale maps for Llama-2-13B, Mistral-7B, and Qwen-7B across 3 representative workloads
Top-line generation quality (ROUGE/ExactMatch/Instr-following) degradation <= 1.5% vs fp16 baseline for targeted prompts
Token-level KL divergence and log-prob delta within thresholds for both greedy and nucleus sampling
Automated rollback path to fp16 when test-suite triggers >2 critical regressions
End-to-end calibration + serve latency impact < 2% p50, and tail latency (p99) increase <= 6%
Calibration runs integrated into nightly CI; metadata and provenance linked to generated scale maps
technical_design: We will compute per-block scale maps (float scalars per weight/activation group per transformer block) using a two-stage approach: (1) robust percentile-based range estimation (e.g., 99.5th trimmed percentile) with optional tail-trim factor; (2) per-head attenuation for attention outputs where head-wise outliers are dominant. Instead of global layer multipliers, store small vectors per-block that adjust quant scales during inference. Calibration artifacts are signed and versioned in the model catalog. Quant kernels will accept optional per-block scale overrides and a fallback flag to use fp16 for blocks marked unstable.
calibration_workflow: 1) Collect representative traces using the production prompt set and synthetic stress prompts (long context, chain-of-thought, repetition). 2) Run robust statistics pass to estimate percentile thresholds and candidate scale maps. 3) Run lightweight perturbation sims (add small noise to triggers) to detect brittle blocks. 4) Generate candidate quant profile with per-block maps and head-clipping rules. 5) Run validation harness (see validation_plan) and compute quality and perf deltas. 6) If regressions exceed thresholds, automatically adjust tail-trim and attenuation parameters and iterate; limit to 3 auto-iterations before flagging for human review.
validation_plan: Validation harness will run three tiers: unit-level numeric checks (per-tensor max error, MSE), functional evaluation (generation metrics: ROUGE, BLEU, Instr-following score), and downstream task checks (chat-turn coherence, reranking accuracy). Use a holdout workload per customer profile (productivity, search, chat) and a public prompt suite. Track: exact-match delta, KL divergence on token distributions, sample-level hallucination rate (heuristic), latency and memory behavior. Store comparison diffs and regression heatmaps per-block.
rollout_plan: 1) Canary: serve quantized model with per-block scale maps to 1% of traffic in a dedicated canary pool (non-critical routes). 2) Observe fidelity, latency, and error counts for 72h. 3) If metrics within thresholds, expand to 10% then 50% over days. 4) Automated rollback triggers: generation-quality regression >1.5% on canary suite, p99 latency > baseline + 10%, or error-rate spike. 5) Document rollout notes and create model catalog entry with calibration provenance, config flags, and contact owner.
monitoring: Per-block numeric drift (max abs error, mean relative error)
Token-level KL divergence vs fp16 baseline (daily aggregates)
Generation quality delta on sampled production prompts (daily)
Latency: p50/p95/p99 and memory usage by model variant
Canary alert that tags model/hash + calibration artifact id on regression
risks_mitigations: Risk: Overfitting calibration to instrumented prompt set -> Mitigation: diversify traces and include adversarial/synthetic prompts
Risk: Per-block overrides increase kernel complexity -> Mitigation: keep map sizes small and fall back to existing fast path when maps are identity
Risk: Unexpected regressions after autoscale iteration -> Mitigation: limit auto-iterations and require human sign-off beyond threshold
Risk: Storage/provenance gaps for calibration artifacts -> Mitigation: sign and version artifacts in model catalog with immutable metadata
comments: 2025-01-16 - Ling Zhang: Initial scoping complete. Chose percentile-trim approach after comparing mean/std and MAD; percentile is more robust to heavy tails on Mistral traces.
2025-01-21 - Carlos Mendes: Implemented prototype that emits per-block scale maps from a 1000-example trace; observed reduced MSE vs single-layer scale baseline on Llama-2-13B.
2025-01-28 - PR #8423: design review feedback from Maya Thompson - asked to clarify fallback semantics and kernel path switch cost. Action: add identity-map fast-path in kernel and microbench it.
2025-02-03 - Performance results: p99 increased by ~4% on initial INT8 run; p50 unchanged. Decided to apply conservative head-clipping (99th) and rerun.
2025-02-07 - QA: Validation harness reported 2/150 critical regressions on Qwen-7B candidate; we increased tail-trim and triggered another calibration iteration.
2025-02-10 - Carlos Mendes: Updated ticket with iteration results; candidate profile now within acceptance thresholds for our internal suite. Preparing canary config and model-catalog entry.
